reading: Standing down or rationalising conventional aids has continued as operators cut cost, at the same time as dependence on GNSS has become the recognised safety risk. Regulators are now working to define minimum operating networks of conventional aids instead
why: This is the defence that actually gets used when interference occurs, and it has been shrinking in the name of efficiency. Every 1 percent rationalised away in a quiet year is one percent of fallback missing in the year it is needed.

label: Single-source income
indicator: Share of household take-home income contributed by the largest single source
reading: ≈60% of take-home pay from one employer
why: Above roughly half, one contract or one bad review cycle is also a cash-flow event, not just an employment event.

label: Emergency runway
indicator: Liquid savings in a separate account divided by monthly essential expenses
reading: ≈2.5 months of essential expenses
why: Below three months, one lost month of pay means selling something, borrowing, or both in the same week.

label: Transferable skill breadth
indicator: Number of distinct tools or capabilities you could be paid for within 30 days
reading: ≈1 distinct billable capability
why: A single capability is a single point of failure wearing a different hat.

label: Notice and severance terms
indicator: Weeks of notice or severance your contract or statute actually guarantees
reading: ≈4 weeks of guaranteed notice
why: Knowing this number before you need it turns a panic into a calculation.

label: Credential reuse
indicator: Count of live accounts still using a password you have typed before
reading: ≈20 reused accounts still active
why: One reused password on a site you forgot about is enough to reach your email, and your email reaches everything else.

label: Reported identity theft
indicator: Identity theft reports filed with the FTC in a year, in millions
reading: ≈1.4 million reports a year
why: Reporting volume is what drives enforcement budgets, so a flat line usually means fewer reports rather than fewer thieves.

label: Credit freeze coverage
indicator: Number of the three US bureaus on which you hold an active freeze
reading: 2 of 3 bureaus frozen
why: A freeze blocks new credit being opened in your name until you lift it — the single highest-leverage hour you can spend.

label: Second-factor coverage
indicator: Accounts protected by an authenticator app or hardware key rather than SMS codes
reading: ≈4 of 40 accounts hardened
why: SMS codes can be forwarded by a SIM swap or read by malware; an authenticator app cannot.

label: Detector coverage
indicator: Working smoke and carbon-monoxide detectors per floor and per sleeping area
reading: 2 of 4 required units installed
why: Undetected fire and carbon monoxide are the two home emergencies where minutes, not hours, decide the outcome.

label: Go-bag currency
indicator: Days since the emergency kit was last restocked and re-checked
reading: ≈420 days since the kit was restocked
why: Water, medication and batteries all expire quietly, so a bag that felt ready quietly stopped being ready.

label: Household plan freshness
indicator: Days since the household emergency plan was last walked through aloud
reading: ≈400 days since the last walkthrough
why: A plan nobody has walked through is a note, and notes do not work under stress.

label: Contents insurance cover
indicator: Contents limit expressed as a multiple of what the home actually holds
reading: ≈0.8× replacement value
why: Underinsurance is the single most common reason a fully covered loss still turns into a personal debt.

label: Personal summary currency
indicator: Months since your one-page medical summary was last updated
reading: ≈26 months since the summary was updated
why: A summary you can hand over in ten seconds is worth more than complete records you cannot produce on demand.

label: Record ownership
indicator: Number of record sources you can retrieve yourself without asking a provider
reading: 2 of 3 record sources reachable online
why: Owning the record means a new doctor, insurer or country can read it without your old provider's cooperation.

label: Wallet card completeness
indicator: Fields completed on your emergency health card, out of allergies, medications, blood type, conditions, contacts
reading: 2 of 5 card fields completed
why: Photographs on a phone die with the phone, and the card is the only version a paramedic can read in seconds.

label: Record retrieval time
indicator: Typical elapsed time for a new clinician to obtain your imaging and labs
reading: ≈21 days typical retrieval time
why: Even improving, weeks is a long time to wait when the decision in front of you is whether to operate.

label: Account inventory currency
indicator: Days since your written account inventory was last updated
reading: ≈400 days since the inventory was updated
why: An inventory from years ago is worse than none, because it looks like coverage while having quietly decayed.

label: Single-point recovery
indicator: Percentage of accounts for which account recovery points to a single email inbox
reading: ≈99% of accounts recover through one inbox
why: One inbox is the whole estate. Lose it, or lose access to it, and everything above it becomes unrecoverable.

label: Named successor coverage
indicator: Count of accounts with a nominated successor or beneficiary registered
reading: 4 of 30 accounts have a named successor
why: Most services offer a successor or legacy-contact field. Filling it in takes two minutes and defaults to nobody.

label: Self-custodied asset clarity
indicator: Wallets, domains and exchange accounts you can name, locate and explain
reading: 2 wallets and 1 domain identified
why: Self-custody gives you control and no support line at all. If nobody else knows what you hold, nobody else can pass it on.

label: Debt service ratio
indicator: Total monthly debt payments as a share of monthly take-home pay
reading: ≈38% of take-home pay going to debt
why: Above roughly a third, one bad month turns into missed payments without you ever deciding to miss them.

label: Cost of your most expensive debt
indicator: Effective annual rate on the largest revolving balance you carry
reading: ≈34-36% APR on the largest balance
why: Above roughly twenty percent, this stops being a budgeting problem and becomes an interest-rate problem.

label: Revolving balance growth
indicator: Change in total revolving card balance over the trailing twelve months
reading: +≈18% over 12 months
why: Rising balances while payments stay flat means you are paying interest every month, not principal.

label: Collection contact
indicator: Third-party collection contacts received in the last twelve months
reading: 0 collection contacts in 12 months
why: The first collection call is the last cheap moment to fix this. After that, reporting and litigation costs appear.
